title: An aligned secondary spin below 0.138 days gives circulation for the fitted TYC 9179-1083-1 state at apsidal constant 0.10
abstract: We test conservative tidal and rotational precession for the published TYC 9179-1083-1 state. Energy and angular momentum give a transition from periapse libration to circulation at secondary spin period 0.13758 days for aligned spins, secondary apsidal constant 0.10, primary constant 0.01, primary spin 10 days and the selected published radius ratios. A 0.12-day secondary spin gives eccentricity 0.159-0.546 and circulation. Slow spins preserve small libration. Independent vector integrations and rate checks support the transition formula. Other published radius ratios shift the threshold to 0.084-0.375 days. No spin is measured. The fast case changes an eight-year eclipse-interval proxy by about 1180 seconds and must be fitted again to measured times. The result is a model sensitivity test, not a viable new orbit or evidence for fast spin. Fixed aligned spins, leading stellar quadrupoles and uncertain radii limit the result. We provide code, fitted parameter inputs, source hashes, simulated trajectories and a figure.

display.caption: Eccentricity under selected spin assumptions and the energy-based transition period. All curves hold the starting dynamical state fixed.
